claim_summary: MOSAIC contributes a memory-grounded financial time-series workflow that profiles data, retrieves prior cases and code, synthesizes and verifies task-adapted models, and refines them with failure-aware offline RL.

claim_evidence.quote: • We introduce a blueprint-based, repository-grounded synthesis framework that retrieves prior cases and source-code modules, extracts reusable components, composes them into executable workflow blueprints, and generates task-adapted implementations.

• We formulate model refinement as a failure-aware offline reinforcement learning problem, where execution feedback, rollback, trajectory branching, and invalid-action masking are used to learn long-horizon refinement policies for LLM-mediated code editing.

modules.name: Semantic-aware time-series profiling
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is no: profiling does not embed a forecast or generation objective. R3_2_GTS is yes: it computes time-series statistics and temporal plots; changing task family leaves the temporal profiling need intact, whereas a non-temporal runtime would not preserve these semantics.

evidence.quote: To bridge the gap between raw numerical data and LLM reasoning, the MOSAIC pipeline begins with a semantic-aware EDA module that maps continuous statistical properties into discrete, text-based semantic anchors.

modules.name: Profile-conditioned prior-case retrieval
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is no: retrieval serves both task families without implementing either output criterion. R3_2_GTS is yes: the query uses the temporal data profile; changing task family preserves this retrieval interface, while removing temporal profile evidence changes what the case match means.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - not bound to one task output

evidence.quote: It is used to query the case bank Ecase and retrieve prior tasks with similar data characteristics, objectives, and evaluation requirements.

modules.name: Repository-grounded blueprint model synthesis
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is no: the same pipeline (architecture-family analysis, AST module extraction, blueprint construction, code generation) is applied unchanged to forecasting and generation; no output requirement or objective of one task family is embedded in its logic, and the retrieved repository is just the source of modules. R3_2_GTS is no: it composes neural-network code modules and shape constraints with no dependence on timestamps, windows, frequency or information availability. R3_3_GH is yes: it is plan construction and code synthesis orchestration.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - same procedure for both task families
R3_2_GTS:no - no temporal semantics in composition logic
R3_3_GH:yes - blueprint planning and code synthesis

evidence.quote: Beyond selecting from a fixed model bank, the model generation module balances retrieval and innovation: it identifies relevant existing models while using LLMs to recombine their components into new executable architectures

Given the module representations and the composition strategy determined above, the system constructs a structured blueprint by jointly considering the task profile, upstream data analysis results, and retrieved prior cases.

modules.name: Candidate execution verification and repair
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is no: this checks executable output shape and numerical stability rather than task quality. R3_2_GTS is no: it has no temporal-order, window, or information-cutoff check. R3_3_GH is yes: it executes candidates, diagnoses failures, and schedules bounded correction.

evidence.quote: Each generated candidate undergoes execution based validation. The system dynamically loads the generated code, instantiates the model with appropriate task dimensions, and performs a forward pass to verify output shape consistency and numerical stability.

modules.name: Task-generation and failure-aware trajectory corpus
modules.scope_reason: R2: the generated tasks and the branched trajectories with negative supervision and invalid-action masks are offline training data built to train the refinement policy, so they are LLM side (workflow_learning); R3 does not apply. The two parts only function together as one corpus.

evidence.quote: We employ an automated task-generation module to construct diverse, executable time-series forecasting and generation tasks, forming a scalable corpus of tasks that can be converted to trajectory data for offline RL of refinement policies.
The failure branch is retained as negative supervision, while the continuation branch records the subsequent valid search from the restored checkpoint.

modules.name: Failure-aware offline refinement policy
modules.scope_reason: R2 classifies the trained policy that selects refinement actions from execution and validation feedback on the model side; the LLM executor is separate. This learned policy is trained for the two task-specific losses, while R3 applies only to Harness mechanisms.

evidence.quote: train a refinement policy on this dataset using offline RL

modules.name: Online refinement execution and recovery loop
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is no: the harness executes the selected edit and reports diagnostics, while the task-specific loss and action policy determine the objective. R3_2_GTS is no: its recovery logic does not depend on temporal ordering or information availability. R3_3_GH is yes: it coordinates execution, rollback, masking, and the next policy query.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - task objective is outside the execution loop
R3_2_GTS:no - no temporal semantics in recovery logic

evidence.quote: The selected action is realised by the LLM executor, the resulting code is executed, and the diagnostics are updated. If the edit triggers a hard failure or soft revert, MOSAIC restores the last valid checkpoint, adds the failed action to the dynamic mask, and queries the policy again.

process_validity.quote: MOSAIC maintains a 100% success rate across all configurations, whereas DS-Agent drops to 60% on multiple datasets.

temporal_validity.quote: We evaluate on three financial datasets spanning different asset classes, frequencies, and data regimes. All datasets are split chronologically (70%/15%/15%) to prevent look-ahead bias.

task_performance.quote: We follow prior work [9] and report standard forecasting metrics, including RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and sMAPE, as well as generation metrics, including Marginal, Correlation, Autocorrelation, and Covariance distances.

decision_utility.quote: We also report ∆VaR and ∆ES on Crypto, ∆Sharpe for forecasting, and system-level Success Rate.

items.reason: Blueprint construction applies one procedure to both task families and composes code modules using shape constraints; it embeds no task-family output criterion and no temporal semantics, so R3_1 and R3_2 fail and R3_3 holds.
An IQL policy is trained offline to select refinement actions from execution feedback; R2 places a trained policy on the LLM side.
